input: I'm enrolling in the HDHP as a single filer (Team Member Only). How much does GitLab contribute to my HSA each month?
golden: As of April 1, 2026, GitLab contributes $125 per month to your HSA for Team Member Only (individual) coverage on the HDHP plan — raised from the previously published $100/month figure. The us-benefits-overview handbook page still shows the old $100/month number but PlanSource is already applying the new amount. You must be enrolled in the HDHP to be eligible, and HSA contributions are taxable at the state level in California, Alabama, and New Jersey.

input: How many weeks of paid parental leave does GitLab offer?
golden: Effective April 1, 2026, GitLab Paid Parental Leave is 20 weeks of fully paid leave (raised from the previously published 16 weeks). The parental-and-other-leave handbook page still shows 16 weeks because the MR has not yet merged. Pay remains 100% of weekly wages, leave can still be split into up to 3 segments, and it must still be used before the child's first birthday or the first anniversary of adoption. USA/Canada team members submit to Tilt 30-45 days before leave.

input: As a US team member using my Navan corporate card, what is the single-charge receipt threshold? Do I need to upload a receipt for a $62 client dinner?
golden: The US single-charge receipt threshold was raised from $50 to $75 effective March 20, 2026. A $62 client dinner is below the new $75 threshold, so no receipt is required. input: What is the current mental health benefit vendor at GitLab and how many therapy sessions does it cover?
golden: GitLab migrated from Modern Health to Spring Health on April 1, 2026. Each team member gets 12 free therapy sessions per calendar year (up from 8 with Modern Health), plus unlimited coaching, a meditation library, and dependent coverage for household members aged 13+. Sign in at gitlab.springhealth.com with your GitLab email using the activation code sent by benefits@gitlab.com. The separate EAP through New York Life (3 face-to-face sessions) is unchanged.

input: Can I expense a ChatGPT Plus subscription, and what are the rules for using AI tools with GitLab data?
golden: Yes — as of April 5, 2026, individual AI tool subscriptions up to $50/month per team member are pre-approved and can be expensed through Navan under the new "AI Tools" category, with no Zip request or Security/Privacy review required. The pre-approved list includes ChatGPT Plus/Team, Claude Pro/Max, Gemini Advanced, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Perplexity Pro. Data rules: no customer data, no unreleased source code, and no personnel data in any prompt. Summaries, public docs, and your own work-in-progress writing are allowed. Violations are reviewed by Security.

input: I've been summoned for jury duty on a potential 4-week trial. How much paid leave do I get, and how do I log it?
golden: GitLab provides up to 30 working days of paid jury-duty / legal civic obligation leave per authorized leave (raised from 25 working days effective March 25, 2026). A 4-week trial is well within the cap. Pay is 100% of weekly wages. Log it in Workday under Time-Off → Jury Duty and attach a copy of your summons. The leave is available from day one of employment and runs concurrently with other job-protected or income-replacement leave as required by law. If your service exceeds 30 working days, email leaves@gitlab.com for case-by-case review.

input: What's the maximum duration of short-term disability coverage at GitLab, and what percentage of my salary does it replace?
golden: GitLab provides short-term disability insurance at no cost to employees. It replaces up to 66.7% of base salary for qualifying disabilities, with a maximum benefit period of 26 weeks. To apply, contact Absence Management at leaves@gitlab.com to submit a Short-Term Disability application. Within 3 business days, New York Life (NYLife) contacts you for additional information if needed, then issues a decision. Absence Management files all paperwork in Workday.

input: I was called up for a 9-month military deployment. After service ends, how long do I have to apply for reinstatement at GitLab?
golden: For military leave exceeding 180 days (9 months qualifies), you have 90 days from the end of service to apply for reinstatement at GitLab. The "escalator principle" applies — you return to the position you would have attained if you had not been called to serve. Unpaid military leave can extend up to 6 months, after which you are offboarded but remain eligible for reinstatement. Healthcare may be retained at your own expense for up to 2 years or end of service, whichever comes first; otherwise benefits end on day 31. Stock vesting continues during up to 6 months of unpaid military leave.
